methodological_eligibility.evidence_quote: An approved energy performance indicator (EnPI) methodology was integrated in the libraries of AML in order to simplify and shorten the modeling procedure for the optimization task.

stage1.ineligibility_reason: Tool/modeling-language design. The paper's own contribution is integrating an externally developed EnPI methodology (Grabowski et al. [4]) as semantic role categories into AutomationML libraries plus a parser-driven optimization workflow (EnEffIPK [6]), demonstrated on an industrial cooling system. It does not present or characterise an EnPI/EnB measurement model itself (no baseline, no normalisation relationship, no functional form, no construction/estimation approach given in-paper), so it falls under the tool/software-without-measurement-model exclusion. BORDERLINE: a reviewer could instead call it eligible-but-empty; routed for human adjudication.

paper_type.evidence_quote: An extension of the established standard allows for intuitive modeling of energy optimization problems.

stage1.notes: Borderline eligibility: AML modeling-language extension integrating a borrowed EnPI methodology; no in-paper EnPI/EnB model characterised. Case sector = industrial cooling/refrigeration (NOT in closed 3B list), so not Corpus B under any reading.
